stem.text: The Michaelis–Menten constant, $K_\text{m}$, is the substrate concentration at which an enzyme works at half its maximum rate.
What is correct when the $K_\text{m}$ value is low?

A.text: The enzyme has a low affinity for the substrate and the quicker the reaction will proceed to its maximum rate.

B.text: The enzyme has a low affinity for the substrate and the slower the reaction will proceed to its maximum rate.

C.text: The enzyme has a high affinity for the substrate and the quicker the reaction will proceed to its maximum rate.

D.text: The enzyme has a high affinity for the substrate and the slower the reaction will proceed to its maximum rate.
